Two geometries from `files/`: toluene, which is symmetric, and a C1 organic molecule with two methyl groups.

**Files used** (from the repository):

* `files/tol.xyz` — toluene C7H8
* `files/nmr.xyz` — C14H17N3O, no symmetry

**1. Toluene**, 0-based indices.

```bash
frog-nmr-equiv files/tol.xyz
```

```text
ℹ  Analyzing equivalencies for: files/tol.xyz
ℹ  Global Point Group: C2v (RMSD: 0.0017 Å)
           Equivalencies (tol.xyz)
╭──────┬───┬───────────────────┬─────────────╮
│ Elem │ N │ Indices (0-based) │ Note        │
├──────┼───┼───────────────────┼─────────────┤
│ C    │ 2 │ 0, 2              │             │
│ C    │ 1 │ 1                 │             │
│ C    │ 2 │ 3, 5              │             │
│ C    │ 1 │ 4                 │             │
│ C    │ 1 │ 6                 │             │
│ H    │ 2 │ 7, 8              │ CH2         │
│ H    │ 2 │ 9, 11             │ CH2         │
│ H    │ 1 │ 10                │             │
│ H    │ 3 │ 12, 13, 14        │ Rotor / Sym │
╰──────┴───┴───────────────────┴─────────────╯
```

* The heavy-atom point group is C2v. C 0/2 and C 3/5 are the ortho and meta ring carbons, and H 7/8 and
  H 9/11 the ortho and meta protons. C 1 (ipso), C 4/H 10 (para) and the methyl carbon C 6 are unique.
* The three methyl H 12, 13, 14 form one group (`Rotor / Sym`), because they rotate freely. The `CH2`
  label on the ring pairs only means "two equivalent H".
* In ¹H NMR, toluene should therefore show four signals: ortho 2H, meta 2H, para 1H and CH₃ 3H.

**2. A molecule without symmetry**, as CSV with 1-based indices (the numbering of `frog-nmr` labels),
keeping only the groups with more than one atom.

```bash
frog-nmr-equiv files/nmr.xyz --one-based --format csv -q | awk -F, 'NR<=2 || $2>1'
```

```text
# Equivalencies (nmr.xyz)
Elem,N,Indices (1-based),Note
H,3,"15, 16, 17",Rotor / Sym
H,3,"19, 20, 21",Rotor / Sym
```

The molecule is C1, so every atom is its own group except the H of the two methyl groups (atoms 15–17
and 19–21, 1-based). These are the only averages `frog-nmr` applies when it simulates the spectrum
of this geometry.
